finding.claim: PUT /doc/<doc_id> performs no authorization check: can_edit() result is discarded, so any user can overwrite the body of any document.
finding.source: docs.py:16-17 route PUT /doc/<doc_id>; doc_id from URL and body from request.json (docs.py:20)

trace.note: DOCS[doc_id] loads any document by ID with no ownership scoping
can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated but return value discarded; can_edit never aborts (docs.py:7-8)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns bool only; result unused at docs.py:19. Sibling route /title uses require_edit (docs.py:11-13, 27) which aborts 403 and is SAFE. g.user is not set in this repo, so whether unauthenticated callers reach the route is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool and never aborts; its result is discarded by the bare call at docs.py:19. require_edit (docs.py:11-13), which aborts with 403, is not called in update_doc; it is only used by update_title at docs.py:27. No other check sits between the request and the write at docs.py:20.
verdict.reason: The bare call `can_edit(g.user, doc)` at docs.py:19 discards its bool result, so the unconditional write at docs.py:20 runs for any caller whose g.user is set, while the sibling route at docs.py:27 correctly uses require_edit. Exploitability assumes an upstream auth layer populates g.user for ordinary authenticated users, as the sibling route also assumes; if g.user is never set, the route raises AttributeError and the write never happens.
